stories.headline: Hormuz Strait closure triggers Norwegian fuel shortage warnings and maritime response
stories.summary: PM Støre warned of potential fuel shortages linked to the Iran war's disruption of Strait of Hormuz shipping, stating Norway's reserves (20 days vs. 90 days for Sweden/Finland) were insufficient, and that measures including work-from-home and rationing could be considered. Norway simultaneously joined an international initiative led by France and the UK with 49 countries to secure free navigation through the strait, exploring a Norwegian contribution to a maritime operation.

stories.headline: Zelenskyy visits Oslo: Norway and Ukraine sign defense declaration, launch drone deal
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy visited Oslo on April 14, meeting PM Støre and Crown Prince Haakon. The two countries signed a Joint Declaration on Enhanced Defense and Security Cooperation, including a drone production arrangement whereby Ukraine will produce drones in Norway while sharing data with Oslo. The visit also surfaced controversy over parts removed from donated Norwegian F-16s before transfer.

stories.headline: Stoltenberg in Washington: defends NATO, GPFG stays in US markets, co-hosts Ukraine donors meeting
stories.summary: Finance Minister and former NATO Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg made a high-profile Washington visit during IMF/World Bank spring meetings, visiting the oil fund's New York office, defending NATO's value to the US amid Trump threats, stating the GPFG has no plans to divest from US assets, and co-hosting with German FM Klingbeil a Ukraine donor support meeting. Stoltenberg also warned that NATO's survival over the next ten years is not guaranteed.

stories.headline: FrP reaches 17-year polling high as Listhaug positions as alternative PM
stories.summary: Sylvi Listhaug's Fremskrittspartiet reached nearly 30 percent in multiple April polls — the party's best result in 17 years — driven in part by the fuel price and Hormuz debates where Listhaug attacked the government's preparedness. Sp's Toppe said her party fears a Listhaug premiership, while commentary discussed the parliamentary arithmetic that could topple Støre.

stories.headline: Government coalition on the edge: MDG threatens to topple Støre, Sp warned against further budget breaches
stories.summary: MDG leader Arild Hermstad said publicly he is willing to let the Støre government fall if the upcoming revised budget fails to deliver on climate commitments. Simultaneously, Støre warned Senterpartiet against repeating its earlier breach of the multi-party budget agreement, and confirmed holding bilateral meetings with both Sp and MDG leaders that week.

stories.headline: Norges Bank rate hike controversy: LO attacks central bank independence, political parties pile in
stories.summary: LO chief Kine Asper Vistnes publicly warned Norges Bank not to raise interest rates, arguing it would undermine wage settlements — triggering a multi-party political melee. Norges Bank governor Ida Wolden Bache said the bank would not be swayed, Stoltenberg defended central bank independence, PM Støre declined to back the LO's criticism, and FrP attacked the government from the other direction. Norges Bank has signalled one or two rate hikes in 2026.

stories.headline: Epstein files shake Norway: parliamentary investigation launched into foreign office connections
stories.summary: The release of the Epstein files has prompted a Norwegian parliamentary investigation into the foreign ministry's connections to Jeffrey Epstein, after senior diplomatic figures including Mona Juul were named. The Guardian reported Norway's parliament oversight committee head said the files had shaken faith in democracy. FM Barth Eide said UD will continue mapping Juul's contacts even after her departure. Separately, researcher Hilde Henriksen Waage accused PM Støre of lying about her and the suppressed Oslo Process documents.

stories.headline: Norway nominates Iran to UN human rights committee, drawing FrP outrage
stories.summary: It emerged that Norway quietly co-nominated Iran to a UN Committee for Economic and Social Rights, which advises on human rights, women's rights, disarmament, and counter-terrorism. FrP leader Listhaug described it as unbelievable and demanded answers from Støre. The government defended the nomination as procedural, noting no other candidate ran.

stories.summary: Foreign Minister Barth Eide publicly praised US President Trump's announcement of a Lebanon-Israel ceasefire, calling it an important and necessary step. He was subsequently criticised domestically for failing to mention Israel's role in the statement, with some calling it predictably one-sided.

stories.headline: Equinor sells Scatec solar stake, signalling continued pullback from renewables
stories.summary: Equinor sold an 8.07 percent stake in Norwegian solar developer Scatec for approximately NOK 1.6 billion, halving its holding to just over 8 percent. The move was widely interpreted as part of Equinor's ongoing capital discipline pivot away from renewables toward higher-return oil and gas, prompting analyst speculation about whether a similar sale of its Orsted stake could follow.

stories.headline: Equinor Q1 trading profit to exceed guidance on Iran war energy volatility; shares swing on Hormuz ceasefire
stories.summary: Equinor announced its Q1 Marketing, Midstream and Processing division profit would exceed the $400 million guidance, partly driven by Middle East war-linked energy price volatility and European gas optimisation. Shares then fell sharply — over 7–10 percent — when the Hormuz Strait ceasefire was announced and crude prices dropped, reducing the geopolitical premium.

stories.headline: GPFG lifts Syria bond ban; backs BP chair against shareholder climate resolutions
stories.summary: Norway's $2.2 trillion Government Pension Fund Global made two notable investment decisions this week: it lifted a longstanding ban on investments in Syrian government bonds, marking Syria's further re-entry into global finance; and it announced it will vote to re-elect BP Chair Albert Manifold and support the board's move to withdraw earlier climate reporting resolutions at the April 23 BP AGM, drawing climate criticism.

stories.headline: Telenor sued for allegedly handing Myanmar military data used to arrest 1,200 activists
stories.summary: A lawsuit filed in Norway alleges that state-linked telecoms firm Telenor passed subscriber data to Myanmar's military junta following the 2021 coup, enabling the arrest of approximately 1,200 activists including some in safe houses. Calls for government accountability are growing, with the government acknowledging 27 meetings with Telenor officials between the coup and the company's exit.

stories.headline: Norwegian defence official and company director charged by Økokrim over Ukraine supply contracts
stories.summary: Norway's financial crimes authority Økokrim charged a Norwegian Armed Forces officer and a company director in connection with alleged misuse of public authority related to Nansen Programme payments for equipment destined for Ukraine. Separately, VG won the Skup prize for its earlier investigation exposing defective gas masks bought for Ukraine under a 100 million kroner contract.

stories.headline: Government quarter reopens 15 years after Breivik bombing
stories.summary: PM Støre and government ministers marked the return to the rebuilt government quarter on April 13, fifteen years after Anders Behring Breivik's bomb destroyed much of the area. Six ministries and approximately 2,200 employees moved back in; minor logistical complaints about missing coffee machines and sparkling water attracted satirical coverage.

stories.headline: Norway pledges 470 million kroner in humanitarian aid to Sudan; Barth Eide attends Berlin conference
stories.summary: FM Barth Eide attended an international ministerial conference on Sudan in Berlin on the third anniversary of the war's outbreak and announced Norway would provide NOK 470 million in humanitarian and long-term assistance to Sudan in 2026. Norway also expressed support for a ceasefire process.

stories.headline: Norwegian Armed Forces contain Israeli-made components in key weapons systems
stories.summary: Forsvarets forum reported that several of Norway's most important weapons systems — including F-35 fighter jets, tanks, and frigates — contain sub-systems and parts from Israeli companies. Defence Minister Tore O. Sandvik said Norway neither buys standalone Israeli weapons systems nor sells weapons to Israel, but removing Israeli components would make building up Forsvaret and NATO integration impossible.

stories.headline: Norwegian Armed Forces: new naval vessel design contract awarded; Parliament scrutinising spending overruns
stories.summary: The Forsvarsmateriell agency awarded a design contract for Norway's new standardised naval vessel class — described as one of the largest maritime investments in Norwegian history — to the Salt/Kongsberg consortium. Separately, Stortinget's control committee opened a formal scrutiny into defence procurement rules compliance, and Høyre pressed the government over its decision to delay long-range air defence procurement from 2029 to 2033.

stories.headline: Støre's food queue comment triggers criticism from Salvation Army and KrF
stories.summary: During a parliamentary question session, PM Støre said that food distribution queues do not necessarily indicate social distress, drawing sharp reactions from the Salvation Army and KrF, who said the remark did not reflect what they see in practice. Støre subsequently sought to nuance his statement.

stories.headline: Vår Energi and Equinor file revised development plan for Goliat gas export project in Barents Sea
stories.summary: Vår Energi (65% operator stake) and Equinor (35%) submitted a revised Plan for Development and Operation for the Goliat Gas Export project to the Norwegian Ministry of Energy. The $360 million investment aims to boost oil output from the Goliat field from 2029 and extend productive life by approximately ten years, with gas to be piped to Equinor's Hammerfest LNG facility.
